NEW DRAFT ASSERTION. Let C be complete algebraically closed, nontrivially real-valued, characteristic/residue-characteristic zero; R=C-circle; 0<|varpi|<1. Actual pair and horizontal Cartier proof. Choose an original integral very ample dL and original nonzero S0; div(S0)=sum n_p p and dL=O(div(S0)) through THIS section. Isolate its one residual etale root by a principal localization of norm one at p. For EVERY j, FK I5.3.10–11 makes B_j etale over the appropriate localization of (R/varpi^j)[t]. Q_j=B_j/(t-c) is affine etale over R_j with the actual evaluation section. Spec R_j has ONE point and nil maximal ideal, possibly without uniform exponent; the extended ideal is nil as each element has finitely many nil coefficients. Thus Spec Q_j has one point. An etale affine section is open and closed by Stacks024T; its image contains that point, hence Q_j=R_j via the given evaluation. Monic t-c is regular over R_j[t], remains regular by flat etale base change, and separation proves regularity in B. For h in ker epsilon its unique quotient by t-c modulo every varpi^j is compatible; completeness gives h=(t-c)q in B. Therefore ker epsilon=(t-c) is closed and B/(t-c)=R. Glue these identical local evaluation ideals with units off the mark to obtain actual horizontal Cartier H_p, generic zero precisely p, residual intersection length one. H=sum n_p H_p has SAME generic dL and residual degrees A_v>=0, sum A_v=d*deg L.

Actual vertical positivity. On the full connected graph use outgoing Laplacian Delta. The identity -sum h_v Delta h_v=sum_edges (h_w-h_v)^2/ell_e proves kernel constants and image zero-sum. Solve Delta h=Q-A for positive vertex degrees Q summing d*deg L. Approximate GLOBAL shared heights by g_v in divisible dense Gamma=-log|C^x|. On each oriented edge choose rational p<s=(g_w-g_v)/ell<q close to the original slope. Bend at t=(q*ell-(g_w-g_v))/(q-p), an actual Gamma-coordinate II point, using p then q. Endpoints agree EXACTLY; new degree q-p>0. Outgoing errors smaller than min Q/(4 max valence) preserve all old positive degrees. Loops use equal shared endpoint heights and count both incidences; every cycle remains.

Clear slopes with N. On a vertex open choose c_v with -log|c_v|=N*g_v; on actual xy=b node choose f_e=c_v*x^m, m the integer outgoing slope. Overlap ratios x^m and (c_v*b^m/c_w)*y^(-m) are integral units: the scalar has norm one by the exact endpoint relation. Cycles require unit ratios, not literal equality of constants. These actual Cartier factors give a vertical bundle with weight N*g at EVERY generic point and degree N*Delta g(v), with signs +m and -m at its two branches. A=O(H)^N tensor O(V_g) has SAME generic d*N*L, positive on ALL old/new components and sum degree N*d*deg L.

Whole-mod-varpi recognition. Each X_j=F mod varpi^j is flat fp over R_j. It is proper, either by actual formal properness or Stacks0BPG(8) on the exact nil-thickening fibre square; no globally nilpotent ideal is asserted. Proper FIELD curve component positivity implies ample fibre by whole Stacks33.44.15. GENERAL37.50.3/0D2S, with proper X_1 and invertible A_1, yields ampleness on its entire one-point base. Noetherian30.21.4 is NOT applied directly to R_1.

Express R_1 as the filtered union of finite Z-subalgebras B_i. The affine inverse-limit hypotheses hold. Whole01ZM descends finite affine presentations, overlaps/equalities and X_1; 0B8W descends the invertible bundle, inverse and evaluation isomorphism; 081F and04AI descend properness and locally-fp flatness. In09MT align finitely many positive section powers to a common multiple BEFORE descending their affine nonvanishing cover. That bounded NONNEGATIVE Čech complex has flat terms over B_i: intersections are affine by separatedness; base-flat rings with invertible modules are flat. CLDv1 germ-bundle6.5.1/6.6.8, support6.9.2 and AC coefficient6.9.4 INCLUDING entire6.9.5 calibration then give genuine curve coefficient deg(A|C_v), value index one. notes.text:
NEW DRAFT CURVE INVERSE over the complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued C of n2. Put a=deg L. Choose n2's actual positive pure-FS reference theta_*, final finite skeleton Gamma0 retaining every cycle, and genuine mu0 of mass a positive at every component vertex. Fix a vertex xi with positive atom. Let mu be ANY positive Radon measure on the entire curve of raw mass a satisfying the intrinsic all-E1 integrability condition of n1. By M, J_theta*(mu) is finite; bounded reference covariance, not a moment at the new reference, justifies this choice.

Actual cofinality. Order actual finite BPR skeleta Gamma_j containing Gamma0 by enlargement. Whole5.2 identifies compact Hausdorff X_an with their inverse limit INCLUDING typeI/IV; whole5.1 puts all II/III on finite graphs. Complement balls make enlargement subdivide the core and attach trees; no cycle is discarded. Retractions are compatible. Continuous factor functions form a min/max lattice containing constants and separating points. For fixed x,y a graph function can take f(x),f(y); finite minima using compactness in y and finite maxima using compactness in x approximate ANY continuous f uniformly. All factors lie on one common graph, so ||f composed r_j-f|| tends to zero uniformly. Therefore mu_j=r_j*mu converges weakly to mu without countable cofinality or support restriction.

Grounded graph kernel. On a finite connected metric graph let j_xi(x,y) have value zero at xi and Delta_out,x j=delta_xi-delta_y. The negative outgoing conductance matrix has grounded positive-definite minor by the sum-of-squared-edge-differences identity. Its inverse is symmetric; the minimum principle gives nonnegative kernel. Subdivision, linear interpolation and the elementary series/contraction law show bounded joint continuity for moving source/test points; loops count both incidences. Attaching a tree at b adds exactly the length of the COMMON initial path from b when both points are in that SAME tree, on top of the old kernel at the retractions. Outgoing sums and grounded uniqueness prove this formula. Pullbacks j_j(x,y)=j_xi(r_j x,r_j y) are bounded jointly continuous and increase on all X_an squared. J0(x)=integral j_j(x,v)dmu0(v) is independent of j, bounded continuous and factors through Gamma0. Set I00=integral J0 dmu0.

Actual finite inverse MUST precede use of O. For a finite positive atomic target nu of mass a on II points of Gamma_j, insert these points as actual vertices and mix an arbitrarily small positive vertex measure so EVERY vertex has strictly positive target weight. Solve Delta h=nu-mu0 with h(xi)=0. Twist the actual reference bundle representing D*L using n2's shared-Gamma heights and rational upward bends applied to D*h. Clear the full slope denominator N; the bundle has SAME generic D*N*L and positive degree on ALL old/new components. n2 supplies actual original algebraic FS recognition with full D*N*k, and its canonical-field/CLD computation supplies genuine raw MA coefficients. These metrics approximate h uniformly; old weights tend to nu and finitely many new bend weights tend to zero.

Choose uniform errors <=2^(-m) and add shifts 4*2^(-m). Shift drops exceed successive errors, so these genuine weighted FS metrics decrease uniformly to h. It is an ACTUAL continuous psh endpoint, bounded and hence E1. Only THEN O's decreasing law identifies its genuine MA with nu. Joint kernel continuity and the same uniform FS extraction remove the positive-vertex mixing. Arbitrary Radon nu on the fixed graph may be NONATOMIC: partition into small Borel pieces and move their masses to nearby actual II points, dense on each edge. The uniform potential error is at most a times the joint kernel oscillation. Diagonal uniform FS extraction again gives an actual continuous endpoint h_nu and genuine MA=nu. The continuous graph potential is never declared psh before this recognition.

In particular u_j(x)=-integral j_j(x,y)dmu(y)+J0(x) is actual continuous theta_*-psh with genuine MA(u_j)=mu_j. It has u_j(xi)=0, upper bound J0 and decreases at EVERY point. Define I_j(nu,eta)=double integral j_j dnu deta and C0=integral J0 dmu, independent of j. These are finite finite-graph integrals. The GENUINE curve energy identity, applied after the metric construction, gives
E(u_j)=(I00-I_j(mu,mu))/2,
integral u_j dmu=-I_j(mu,mu)+C0,
F_mu(u_j)=(I_j(mu,mu)-2*C0+I00)/2.
The total mass throughout is raw a. Finite J bounds I_j(mu,mu)<=2*J+2*C0-I00, hence the energies have a uniform finite lower bound. No moment-only coercivity is invoked.

Set u=inf_j u_j. The finite anchor zero excludes the identically -infinity endpoint. To prove actual FS membership without net-flattening or minimum-of-FS assumptions, let A consist of genuine FS scalars phi with phi>=u+delta EVERYWHERE for some delta>0. Uniform approximation of one u_j plus a positive shift makes A nonempty. For any finite prior list, let delta be its smallest gap. Directed open sets {u_j<min phi_l-delta/2} cover compact X_an. One j gives the inequality everywhere; an FS approximation with error<delta/16 plus delta/8 is below all prior members and still has a positive gap above u. Thus A is downward directed. Arbitrarily close approximations of u_j show inf A=u. Each phi in A dominates some u_j by the same compact-open-cover argument, so E(phi) has the uniform lower bound above. O's EXTENDED energy continuity on this literal FS net, BEFORE E1, gives E(u)>-infinity. Now apply O's E1 decreasing-net genuine MA law to u_j downarrow u and the weak target limit: MA(u)=mu on SAME original L.

After this ACTUAL inverse, and only after it, M's known-output supporting inequality gives variational attainment. Existence bypasses arbitrary-envelope orthogonality and compactness of the full normalized potential cone by actual finite-graph inversion, uniform retraction tests, the finite-dual raw bound and literal FS-net construction. The argument includes all genera, all branches and unrestricted intrinsic target support. It does not provide a higher-dimensional inverse. This proof is written fully in P16.4-argument.md/P16.4-paper.tex and remains unverified.

notes.text:
NEW DRAFT every-solution/every-point uniqueness and original-field descent for the inverse of n3. It does not assume finite values of every E1 potential at every point.

Finite ACTUAL carrier for every FS test. Let v=phi-theta_* for ANY finite real-weight algebraic FS metric on original L. Clear section/reference degrees together and use a nonzero rational algebraic section as common frame. The finitely many section ratios have finite divisors. Whole BPR marked model/skeleton and5.15, with2.10/2.13 and visually checked BL85 ordinary-node3.1–2, make their log norms factor through the punctured skeleton with integral slopes. Near each marked classical point use a nonvanishing local L-frame and parameter. Each section is parameter to its nonnegative order times a unit of constant norm on a small ball. Basepoint freeness supplies an order-zero section of finite weight, so positive-order terms lose to it sufficiently far down the ray. Both phi and theta_* therefore become flat on that tail. Truncate finitely many rays beyond the last switches at actual II points. v now factors through a FINITE actual skeleton. Real-weight typeIII switches are retained.

For Gamma weights its II vertex heights are in Gamma and slopes are rational with the FULL common degree denominator. Switch positions are Gamma-coordinate II points. Pull back the actual reference formal bundle and build n2's SIGNED vertical Cartier factors, clearing the full original scalar/reference denominator. The generic bundle remains the original one and the metric equals theta_*+v at EVERY point. It was ALREADY FS; no strict-positive recognition theorem is needed for this test. n2's actual canonical residual fields and signed genuine CLD coefficients give Delta_out v=MA(v)-mu0. Zero-degree refinement vertices are allowed in this signed curvature calculation. On any fixed Gamma_j enlarge to the carrier and collapse attached trees: internal outgoing incidences cancel, total true curvature appears at the attachment, and flat outer tails contribute zero. Grounded graph uniqueness gives, for x in Gamma_j,
v(x)-v(xi)=-integral j_j(x,y)dMA(v)(y)+J0(x).
For arbitrary real weights approximate by Gamma weights uniformly; bounded nearby weights admit a COMMON far tail truncation. Genuine continuous MA is uniformly-to-weak continuous. The bounded jointly continuous kernel passes the displayed trace identity without an unsupported edge-derivative convergence claim. Thus it holds for EVERY real-weight FS scalar.

Let v be ANY actual E1 solution of the prescribed equation and choose its defining decreasing FS net v_i downarrow v. O's all-test integrability against genuine mu0 with positive atom at xi proves v(xi) finite. This uses E1 of the GIVEN solution, not M's old moment at a changed reference. O gives MA(v_i) weakly to mu. On fixed Gamma_j the family {j_j(x, .):x in Gamma_j} is compact in the uniform norm. A finite epsilon-net and common raw mass reduce uniform convergence of integrals to finitely many weak tests. Passing the trace identity gives v(x)-v(xi)=u_j(x) at ALL x on Gamma_j, hence all II/III points.

Endpoint equality needs more than USC. For each continuous FS v_i, outside Gamma0 the reference curvature is zero, its true curvature is positive, and its adapted carrier has flat tails. Summing the true outgoing curvature in a future subtree gives outward derivative minus the remaining mass, hence <=0. Uniform Gamma-weight passage preserves radial inequalities for real weights. Thus v_i(r_j x)>=v_i(x) for EVERY x,j. Once Gamma_j contains its finite carrier, factorization gives equality, including typeI/IV endpoints. Consequently inf_j v_i(r_j x)=v_i(x), not merely a dense-set or a.e. identity. Commuting the two actual infima of the same doubly indexed set gives
v(x)=inf_i inf_j v_i(r_j x)
    =inf_j inf_i v_i(r_j x)
    =v(xi)+inf_j u_j(x)
    =v(xi)+u(x)
for EVERY analytic point, with literal -infinity values preserved. The constant is finite. This proves EVERY actual E1 solution, including solutions with poles and typeIV limits, agrees modulo a finite constant. It is not inferred from USC, Hilbert uniqueness or comparison alone.

Original-field descent. Let K be ANY original complete nontrivially real-valued characteristic/residue-characteristic-zero field and C its completed algebraic closure. D gives the canonical invariant Radon lift of raw mu and equality of continuous J relative to the pulled-back original continuous reference. M/reference covariance makes it an intrinsic upstairs target. Apply n3 upstairs. The constructed model/theta_* need not be invariant; normalize the ABSOLUTE solution relative to the INVARIANT pulled-back ORIGINAL reference by supremum zero. Its supremum is finite since the actual endpoint is bounded above and nontrivial. Conjugation of genuine continuous FS approximants and O's independence give operator equivariance. Every automorphic image is therefore another E1 solution of the invariant lifted target. The every-solution EVERY-point equality just proved makes its difference a finite constant; the same supremum zero makes that constant zero. The ACTUAL singular metric is invariant BEFORE applying D; no singular averaging is used.

D descends this actual psh/E1 metric to SAME original L; O's singular pushforward yields genuine MA=mu, raw mass a with no field-degree/probability/factorial factor. For any two downstairs solutions, their pulled-back operators are invariant, push to mu, and hence equal D's UNIQUE invariant lift. Apply the upstairs every-point theorem and surjectivity of the quotient to obtain the finite constant equality at EVERY original point. M gives attainment after the inverse. Original trivially valued fields use the already complete T; no genus-zero recap is needed.

Thus the proposed new theorem covers ALL genera and ALL original complete fields for curves, arbitrary-support intrinsic targets and every-solution/all-point uniqueness.
